channel.title: AI Research Intelligence
channel.description: Evidence-grounded daily AI and machine-learning research intelligence.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — September 4, 2026
item.description: Three papers show why AI evaluation must be treated as a measurement supply chain: observers drift, serving adapters censor tool calls, and predictive quality can conceal safety violations.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — September 3, 2026
item.description: Three new papers converge on a practical control-plane design for enterprise agents: reversible data state, measurable causal coverage, and domain-calibrated failure detection.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — September 2, 2026
item.description: September 2, 2026 · Three deep papers, two Watchlist papers · Central signal: an AI control loop cannot validate itself through the same judge it is optimizing against. Reliable long-horizon systems need independent truth lanes, typed trace state, and dependency-aware failure diagnosis.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — September 1, 2026
item.description: Strongest signal: fresh evidence reinforces a deployment lesson: high retrospective discrimination does not establish operational value. Enterprise release gates should measure prevalence-sensitive precision, heterogeneity, external transfer, downstream outcomes, and human reliance—not benchmark score alone.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — August 29, 2026
item.description: Today’s strongest signal is that reliable enterprise AI should bind generation to a stronger decision process: probabilistic uncertainty for choosing experiments, claim-level provenance for synthesizing evidence, and human-centered translation gates before high-stakes adoption. Capability alone is not the control plane.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — August 28, 2026
item.description: Today’s strongest signal is about authority: models can mistake authoritative presentation or tool-provided instructions for permission, while enterprise knowledge systems lose temporal and relational fidelity as scale grows. The architectural response is to separate evidence from authority, execution intent from authorization, and retrieval convenience from verified temporal state.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — August 27, 2026
item.description: The strongest new signal is architectural: enterprise agents need three separate control planes—semantic fidelity, resource-feasible execution, and set-level outcome coverage. A successful run, a valid plan, or a diverse-looking answer set is not sufficient evidence of reliable business value.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — August 26, 2026
item.description: Primary signal: reliable enterprise AI will depend less on “more context” or “more autonomy” than on whether systems can integrate the right evidence, preserve obligations across long workflows, and invoke the right policy at the right moment.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — August 25, 2026
item.description: August 25, 2026 · Newly published research on silent model failure, synthetic-data semantics, forecasting discipline, and AI-agent software quality. Results are author-reported unless explicitly labeled otherwise.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — August 24, 2026
item.description: August 24, 2026 · A deliberately narrow review of new peer-reviewed AI/ML research with enterprise architecture relevance. Research claims are separated from author interpretation and enterprise inference.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — August 21, 2026
item.description: Persistent agent state is moving from “more memory” toward governed state, attributable evidence, agent-ready data, and runtime resource control.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — August 20, 2026
item.description: The strongest signal is architectural: reliable agents need structured substrates, semantics-preserving robustness tests, and deterministic verification boundaries. Model capability alone is not the control plane.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — August 19, 2026
item.description: Today’s strongest research signal is that AI value depends on the interface between machine evidence and human or operational judgment. Machine-discovered strategies can persist through people, but automated selection and safety evaluation fail when their validity assumptions are hidden.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — August 18, 2026
item.description: Today’s research signal is not “better models.” It is the need to make evidence itself governable: contrastive cases must expose response bias, annotator provenance must remain visible, and agent-written facts must carry time, authority, policy, and replayable verdicts.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — August 17, 2026
item.description: Today’s strongest signal: AI reliability must be measured at the granularity where failure occurs—individual requests, evolving environments, and persistent system state—not only through aggregate benchmark scores.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — August 16, 2026
item.description: Today’s strongest signal: consequential AI systems need two different kinds of operational discipline—calibrated decision support at the application layer and workload-aware runtime selection beneath it.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — August 15, 2026
item.description: Today’s strongest signal: enterprise AI reliability depends as much on the execution path, trajectory controls, and inference scheduler as on the model—making those layers measurable is now a practical architectural priority.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — August 14, 2026
item.description: Today’s strongest signal: reliable enterprise AI is shifting from model-centric optimization toward governed composition—semantic resource contracts, domain tools, process-level verification, and human enactment workflows.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — August 13, 2026
item.description: Today’s strongest signal: agent reliability failures increasingly originate in the control plane around the model—skills, retrieved evidence, tool policies, and evaluation design—not merely in model intelligence.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — August 12, 2026
item.description: August 12, 2026 — adaptive research systems are moving from “one model, one context” toward explicit orchestration of research state, reusable skills, and controlled experimental worlds.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — August 11, 2026
item.description: Today’s strongest signal is architectural: agents are becoming more credible when the surrounding system can learn from failures, prove obligations before execution, and diagnose which retained state caused an answer to break .

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — August 10, 2026
item.description: Today’s strongest signal is not another leap in general model capability. It is a shift toward training and evaluating agents against verifiable intermediate evidence : executed statistical tests, clinician-rated longitudinal behavior, and provenance-correct financial retrieval.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — August 9, 2026
item.description: August 9, 2026 · Today’s signal: enterprise AI advantage is moving into the control plane—routing routine work deterministically, adapting serving topology at runtime, and carrying verifiable provenance through the AI supply chain.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — August 8, 2026
item.description: August 8, 2026 · Today’s research signal: agent quality increasingly depends on the reliability of the surrounding system—history, harnesses, evaluation boundaries, and traceable evidence—not model weights alone.

item.title: AI Research Intelligence Brief — August 6, 2026
item.description: Research opportunities: reproduce on H100/B200/TPU and managed cloud; randomize workflow order; publish trace schemas; compare predictive vs hint-driven scheduling; test tenant isolation and adversarial tool bursts; quantify statistical uncertainty; and study cost-aware scheduling under heterogeneous model gateways.

item.description: AI Research Intelligence Brief for August 5, 2026 — visual executive dashboard based on newly submitted arXiv papers.
